inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (222.5M; includes 1.5M incremental share-based awards). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the company is a net repurchaser (count fell 224.9M FY2025 -> 222.5M Q2 2026), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $88.1M (cash-flow add-back $86.6M). Taxes withheld on net-share settlement are not separately tagged in XBRL (folded into 'other financing'); no combined company figure is published, so the expense line is used. Immaterial at ~0.4% of revenue.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.1% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.05 for a premium commercial-HVAC industrial -> cost of equity ~9.4%; debt is ~5% of EV at ~4.5% pre-tax, so WACC ~9.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality and the AI data-center concentration are charged in the bear flows and the weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost already sits inside operating expense, so EBITDA is post-rent (treatment B by construction). Operating lease liabilities ($824.7M at 2025-12-31) are EXCLUDED from net debt; lease_cost_pct_path 0 because the charge is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (operating income incl. NCI share). NCI charged once in the equity bridge at an estimated market value (~15x the ~$27M/yr of dividends paid to NCI), not at the $22M book value.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table: operating company, industrial with moderate cyclicality -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). First valuation of TT; no memory entry. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 2,811.5 (OCF 3,194.5 - capex 383.0) - SBC 88.1 - interest income 0 = 2,723.4. Interest income not stripped: TT is net debt ($3.3B), so the cash is not a material separate pile. Anchors: cash $1,318.3M (cash+restricted, 10-Q 2026-06-30), debt $693.1M current + $3,923.7M non-current = $4,616.8M (2026-06-30). FY0 is FY2025 actual; FY2026 (year 1) is guided ~11.5% reported revenue growth, adj EPS $15.20-15.30 (Q2 2026 call, July 2026). Discounting is end-of-year from FY2025, which is mildly conservative because three quarters of FY2026 have already elapsed. Component calibration: FY2025 operating income 3,967.4 + D&A 376.3 + SBC 88.1 = adj EBITDA 4,431.8 (20.8% of revenue). Working capital: back-solved unlevered owner FCF vs. component NOPAT gives roughly -10% (FY2023), +3% (FY2024), -19% (FY2025) of the revenue change; -8% used. H1 2026 contract liabilities rose $805M (data-center customer advances) -- a one-off FY2026 tailwind deliberately NOT extrapolated. H1 2026 acquisitions $742M already out of cash; any unclosed LiquidStack consideration after 2026-06-30 is not in the bridge (price undisclosed in the data available). Buybacks $1.48B FY2025 vs SBC $88M: the company repurchases far more than grants, so buybacks beyond SBC are capital return funded from owner FCF and are value-neutral here.

equity_bridge.note: ~15x the $26.7M FY2025 dividends paid to NCI (XBRL PaymentsOfDividendsMinorityInterest); book NCI only $22.2M at 2026-06-30

equity_bridge.item: Discontinued operations / legacy asbestos (Aldrich & Murray) cash drain
equity_bridge.note: Discontinued-ops loss $37.0M FY2025 after tax, operating cash outflow $25.9M FY2025; outside continuing operating income so not in the flows. Capitalised at ~12-15x as a run-off liability estimate.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (6.0%) diverges >30% from revenue (11.4%) and EPS (29.8%) CAGRs: book value is suppressed by heavy buybacks ($1.1-1.5B/yr) and dividends, so it is not a usable growth proxy here. EPS 5yr CAGR starts from a COVID-depressed FY2020 ($3.56). Revenue 3yr CAGR selected as the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income nil). Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are within ~1pp, so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow -- SBC is ~0.4% of revenue. FY2022 FCF (1,212) was a working-capital trough (supply-chain inventory build), which flatters the 3yr FCF CAGR.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance (~11.5% reported); the $12.1B backlog (+70% YoY) converts through FY2027 at ~10%, then growth fades to ~3.5% as data-center build rates normalise and residential tracks housing. Margin expands ~160bp over the decade on mix (applied/data-center chillers, services attach), reaching 23% adj EBITDA -- below the incremental-margin framework would imply, because tariffs (~$200M/yr) and competitive entry by Carrier/JCI/Daikin into liquid cooling cap pricing.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2025 20.8%; FY2026 guide implies ~21.4% (Q2 2026 op margin 19.3% + D&A 1.6% + SBC 0.4%).
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: GAAP ETR 19.2% FY2025, 18.7% H1 2026; cash taxes $647M vs $706M provision. 19.5% on EBIT reflects Pillar Two minimums on the Irish-domiciled group.

bull.narrative: AI-factory thermal management becomes a durable new category: 800V DC chillers and LiquidStack direct-to-chip cooling win share in hyperscale builds, so commercial HVAC compounds double-digit through FY2029 while the A2L refrigerant replacement cycle and building electrification lift the installed base and the services annuity. Mix shift to applied systems and services drives adj EBITDA to 24.5%; customer advances keep working-capital drag light.

bear.narrative: Hyperscaler capex digests in 2027-28: data-center orders, which carried the +70% backlog, cancel or push out, and the $805M of customer advances unwind. Commercial HVAC falls mid-single digits in FY2028 while residential suffers a rate-driven housing slump and Thermo King stays in a freight recession. Tariffs and price competition from Carrier/JCI/Daikin in liquid cooling compress adj EBITDA back to ~19-20% (FY2023-24 levels) before a slow GDP-plus recovery on the installed-base service annuity.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance delivered in FY2026, backlog converts at ~10% in FY2027, then growth fades to ~3.5% as data-center build rates normalise; adj EBITDA margin expands ~160bp to 23% on applied-systems and services mix, held back by tariffs and liquid-cooling competition.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI-factory cooling (800V DC chillers, LiquidStack liquid cooling, NVIDIA DSX reference designs) becomes a durable double-digit category through FY2029 on top of the A2L replacement cycle and electrification; margin reaches 24.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hyperscaler capex digestion in 2027-28 unwinds the data-center backlog and customer advances, coinciding with a housing-driven residential slump and freight recession at Thermo King; revenue falls ~4% in FY2028 and margin reverts to ~19-20%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20% because a large share of the record backlog is concentrated in hyperscale data-center capex, a single end-market with a history of digestion cycles. Base 50% as the guidance-anchored path. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs both the AI cooling category and the residential/transport recovery to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF at a 9% USD WACC with SBC fully expensed and a flat diluted count. TT is a high-quality, moderately cyclical compounder whose current multiple prices in sustained double-digit growth; the house value asks what the flows support if data-center demand normalises on a normal cycle.
key_risks_to_valuation: Data-center/AI capex concentration in the backlog -- a hyperscaler digestion cycle hits orders, advances and margins at once
Terminal value is the majority of EV; the 18x base cap and 3% terminal growth carry most of the value
Tariff cost (~$200M/yr after mitigation) and competitive entry into liquid cooling could cap the margin expansion
Legacy asbestos (Aldrich/Murray) and NCI bridge items are estimates, not disclosed fair values
LiquidStack consideration not closed by 2026-06-30 would reduce net cash further
